problem_statement: Backport the upstream JWS critical-header deserialization fix to Authlib 1.6.3. Reject an unsupported critical protected header and a critical header missing from the protected header, while preserving ordinary signed payloads, noncritical private headers, and recognized critical headers.
notes: Selected existing suite: tests/jose/test_jws.py (16 target cases), plus one external compact-JWS security test and three controls; this does not cover the full JOSE or JWT implementation.

Prerequisite: upstream parent eb07119430e7afe52d60f885f9dda3287f80ca6b introduces the critical-header validator and error class absent from 1.6.3. reference.patch includes that ordinary prerequisite implementation plus the selected receiving-side fix, without changing upstream tests.

The eight reviewed fixture SHA-256 pins are retained in harness.toml. They identify public upstream test fixtures, not operator credentials; source snapshots fetch them from the pinned public Git history. No upstream PEM test fixture content is copied into this case bundle or dependency image.

Public fixture provenance: https://github.com/authlib/authlib; tests/files has Git tree 935116faaafff82b7ad83a2462fcaacf0bf3ff87 at target dbbfa9abcfe725001b452cf08d9e48be0ebfdce9, upstream parent eb07119430e7afe52d60f885f9dda3287f80ca6b, and upstream fix 06f0813901a5238dd0b94521d26a7af9064497a0. All three fixture trees are identical.

The Dockerfile starts from the pinned public Python base and installs only hash-locked dependencies. It does not reuse the historical fixture-bridge image, copy fixtures, or monkeypatch fixture reads.
Advisory: https://github.com/authlib/authlib/security/advisories/GHSA-9ggr-2464-2j32. The behavioral oracle accepts the intended JOSE rejection rather than requiring one exception subclass.
